\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{تحقیق} (tahqīq)}{تحقیق (tahqīq)}]{\ur{تحقیق} (tahqīq) — research}

\label{lesson:UR-C349-tahqiq}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to threaten, then the Urdu for to coax.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{تحقیق}}
\textbf{\ur{تحقیق}} — \emph{tahqīq} — \textquotedblleft{}research\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{وہ} \ur{پانی} \ur{پر} \ur{تحقیق} \ur{کر} \ur{رہی} \ur{تھی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{voh pānī par tahqīq kar rahī thī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She was doing research on water.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{تحقیق}} (\emph{tahqīq}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{taḥqīq}, \textquotedblleft{}verification, finding out what is true\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tahqīq}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{voh pānī par tahqīq kar rahī thī.} — She was doing research on water.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to threaten, then the Urdu for to coax, then say \emph{tahqīq} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{کھوجنا} (khojnā)}{کھوجنا (khojnā)}]{\ur{کھوجنا} (khojnā) — to search out; to investigate}

\label{lesson:UR-C349-khojna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a researcher, then the Urdu for a discovery.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{کھوجنا}}
\textbf{\ur{کھوجنا}} — \emph{khojnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to search out; to investigate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{وہ} \ur{اس} \ur{بیماری} \ur{کی} \ur{وجہ} \ur{کھوج} \ur{رہے} \ur{تھے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{voh is bīmārī kī vajah khoj rahe the.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
They were searching out the cause of this illness.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{راز} \ur{کھوجا}, \emph{us ne rāz khojā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{کھوجنا}} (\emph{khojnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{khojnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to seek, to enquire\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*khōjja}, \textquotedblleft{}a footprint\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 3929). To follow a trail of footprints.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}
